name: SORTBY
description: SORTBY returns a dynamic array sorted by the values in one or more separate 'by' arrays, rather than by the array's own columns.
tldr: Sorts an array using other arrays as keys.

parameters.name: array
parameters.description: The range or array to be sorted (returned in the result).

parameters.name: by_array1
parameters.description: The first array of values to sort by; must have dimensions compatible with array.

parameters.name: sort_order1
parameters.description: 1 for ascending (default) or -1 for descending for the first key.

parameters.name: by_array2
parameters.description: An optional additional array to sort by when the first key ties.

parameters.name: sort_order2
parameters.description: Sort order for the second key (1 or -1).

basicExample.description: Sort one column using another as the key
basicExample.result: Values of B2:B10 reordered to match ascending order of A2:A10
basicExample.explanation: SORTBY orders column B by the values in column A ascending.

advancedExamples.title: Sort by multiple keys
advancedExamples.scenario: Sort names by Department ascending, then by Score descending.
advancedExamples.result: Names ordered by department, then by score highest-first within each department
advancedExamples.explanation: The first by_array sets the primary order and the second breaks ties.

advancedExamples.title: Descending by a helper column
advancedExamples.scenario: Sort a list newest-first using a date column.
advancedExamples.result: Items in A2:A10 ordered by dates in B2:B10, newest first
advancedExamples.explanation: sort_order -1 sorts the helper column descending.

howItWorks: SORTBY sorts array according to the values in one or more separate by_arrays. Each by_array has an optional sort_order of 1 (ascending) or -1 (descending); additional by_array/order pairs act as tie-breakers. The by_arrays must share the same height/width as array. The result is a dynamic array that spills into neighboring cells.

howToSteps.name: Pick the result array
howToSteps.text: Choose the range you want returned.

howToSteps.name: Add the key arrays
howToSteps.text: Supply one or more by_arrays and their orders.

howToSteps.name: Ensure spill space
howToSteps.text: Leave empty cells for the spilled result.

limitations: Each by_array must have the same height/width as array.
Cannot sort by a computed expression unless it resolves to an array.

commonErrors.cause: The spill range is blocked by other content.
commonErrors.fix: Clear the cells in the spill area.

commonErrors.cause: A by_array has different dimensions than array.
commonErrors.fix: Make all by_arrays the same size as the array argument.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets does not have a native SORTBY; it uses SORT with an index/order, or SORTN. You can mimic SORTBY by feeding sort columns into SORT.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: In Sheets, multiple sort keys are passed directly to SORT rather than via separate by-arrays.

faq.question: SORTBY vs SORT?
faq.answer: SORTBY sorts by other arrays; SORT sorts the array by its own columns/rows.

faq.question: Is SORTBY in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: No native SORTBY; Sheets uses SORT with index/order arguments.

faq.question: Can I use multiple sort keys?
faq.answer: Yes, supply additional by_array and sort_order pairs.
